content:
In this PR thread, there was some discussion on how to treat the "Mathlib boundary" for future projects.

An example where I encountered this situation was around a decomposition into an infinite union. The easiest overview of that situation is probably the post-upstreaming PR.

Of course in that case we were not going to go through the effort of pre-emptively deriving the general statement; it was totally fine to do this as part of the upstreaming process.
It did, however, take me some time afterwards to retrofit the upstreamed version into the Carleson context, with some unexpected caveats and issues.

Based on my experience and giving this some thought, I would probably go for a process solution instead of defining a boundary upfront. Sometimes the upstreaming retrofit can get convoluted, especially if you would use a result in multiple places (say >2). By the DRY software principle, I would probably like to have a mechanism to:

  1. Initially have stuff in ToMathlib and use it
  2. Go through upstreaming process
  3. Have the option to move the original stuff from ToMathlib (now upstreamed) to NoMathlib or something, and deal with the glue to the upstreamed version there (besides of course the naive option of gluing to Mathlib in-place)
  4. Keep the original context and result the same

This approach solves the issue that there would be things in the ToMathlib folder that are no longer going to be upstreamed, but are still useful in the project context itself.

Thoughts are welcomed on a) if that approach makes sense; b) if it's worth mentioning in the paper. It seems like a small thing so I don't mind either way, but I thought I put it out here anyway so that others can weigh in on its merits.

I have thought about this a lot, and let me summarise my own experience with one rhetorical question: If you need glue between your upstreamed result and your project, have you done a good job upstreaming?
My own answer is often "No", meaning I go back to what I just upstreamed and make it more general or add corollaries

I think that is definitely a valid baseline. There might be edge cases as always, but in general indeed I can see that the need for more than a pinch of glue warrants a (possibly soliloqual) discussion on what to do about that. Possible outcomes would be like you say, and/or to conclude that the original upstreaming candidate was still too rooted in the project. After which the NoMathlib direction remains a possible conclusion.

(On a side note, as a more 'casual' contributor, I experience tribal knowledge and experience to be quite important in the process of upstreaming to Mathlib. If there were some reference/tutorial/handbook, that would definitely make it easier for me to take on more of the work. The current trial-and-error has dissuaded me at times.)
Deciding that something can't be upstreamed amounts to giving up on upstreaming anything that depends on it. As a mathlib maximalist, this is unsatisfying!
And yes I agree, we should write more of this knowledge down. I have been doing bits here and there, but I know of no effort focused on improving the contribution documentation

Jasper Mulder-Sohn said:

(On a side note, as a more 'casual' contributor, I experience tribal knowledge and experience to be quite important in the process of upstreaming to Mathlib. If there were some reference/tutorial/handbook, that would definitely make it easier for me to take on more of the work. The current trial-and-error has dissuaded me at times.)

I strongly agree there are lots of things to be documented. It's just hard work, and there's always a need for more helping hands. Some resources exist already, though. In general terms, there are (for example)

  • the PR review guide (written from the reviewer's perspective),
  • mathlib values document
  • style guide, etc.

About concrete areas, the mathlib phrasebook aims to fill some of the gaps. Much of the remaining stuff is missing!
I thought to mention the phrasebook, but it seems to be more about "how to achieve" rather than "how to contribute". or are contribution guidelines welcome there too?

Yaël Dillies said:

Deciding that something can't be upstreamed amounts to giving up on upstreaming anything that depends on it. As a mathlib maximalist, this is unsatisfying!

In that case, I think something is missing. Something to bridge the gap between the initial "this could be Mathlib material" and the final PR review sitting amidst hundreds of others. A place to discuss things through before vying for a reviewer/maintainer's time, or worse, wasting it (and the contributor's!).

Yaël Dillies said:

I thought to mention the phrasebook, but it seems to be more about "how to achieve" rather than "how to contribute". or are contribution guidelines welcome there too?

No, indeed the phrasebook has a different focus. It can be useful to get up to speed in a particular area, though.
